newsitem.title: USA: Conference Board's Consumer Confidence Index falls.
newsitem.headline: Conference Board's Consumer Confidence Index falls.

text.p: Consumer confidence slipped this month, but the nation's economy is still on track for healthy growth, the Conference Board said on Tuesday.
The private business group said its index of consumer confidence fell to 126.5 in July from June's revised 129.9 figure after back-to-back gains over the prior two months.
Two other key measures -- the expectations component of the index and the present situations index -- also declined in July, but from historically high levels, the Conference Board said.

"Despite the slight decline in consumer confidence this month, both the present situation and expectation indexes are running at historically high levels," said Lynn Franco, associate director of board's Consumer Research Centre.
"While consumer confidence is subject to fluctuations, latest readings continue to signal healthy economic growth ahead," she added.
The expectations component of the index, which has proven to be a key measure of future business activity, fell to 107.6 in July from a revised 111.7 in June.
The present situations index fell to 154.8 in July, down more than two points from June.

While more consumers viewed business conditions in July as "bad" (12 percent vs. 10.5 percent in June), Americans were still optimistic about the job market, the Conference Board said. The proportion of consumers who said jobs were "hard to find" was unchanged from the June level.

There was also a modest downturn in future expectations, the New York-based group said. Less than 17 percent of those surveyed expected business conditions to improve in the months ahead, compared with almost 20 percent in June.
The monthly survey of some 5,000 U.S. households is conducted for the Conference Board by NFO Research Inc. of Greenwich, Conn.
